title: fix(scripts): assert an ADR number names one decision + repair a broken ADR link (#5992)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#5992

Route **C** of the maintainer ruling of 2026-08-07 on that issue, quoted verbatim:

> **Ruling (maintainer, 2026-08-07): C first, B to finish. A is rejected.**
>
> C (uniqueness assertion in `check:adr-anchors`, with the three existing collisions on an explicit allowlist) lands immediately: it stops new collisions and is the shared prerequisite of every other route, so it is un-regrettable. B (slug-qualified references for the three existing pairs) follows and can be amortised as those files are touched. The broken `./0010-metadata-protection.md` link is fixed regardless of route.
>
> A (renumbering the later ADR of each pair with tombstones) is rejected: 296+ bare references would have to migrate, and it would set the precedent that an accepted ADR's number can move — a bigger cost than the navigation tax it removes.

Route B is **not** implemented here and nothing is renumbered. The 328 bare `ADR-0057` references in `packages/**` are untouched.

---

## What changed

**1. `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs` now audits the premise its anchors rest on.**

The file already checked that anchored code still names its ADR. It never checked that the id it names identifies a decision — and for three numbers it does not. The new `auditAdrDirectory()` groups `docs/adr/` filenames by number and fails when one number is claimed by two different decision **stems**.

The three pre-existing pairs sit on `KNOWN_NUMBER_COLLISIONS`, an explicit shrink-only allowlist with per-entry rationale. A fourth collision goes red; a *stale* entry (allowlisted number that no longer collides) goes red too, so a resolved collision cannot silently return under its own grandfather clause; and a **third** record joining an allowlisted pair is a distinct, separately-worded failure — the allowlist grandfathers exactly the pair that existed, it does not licence the number.

**`0006` is not special-cased by name.** The rule that separates it from a real collision is structural: a version repeats the same `NNNN-slug` stem and adds `.vN`, a collision is two different stems under one number. `0006-project-environment-split{,.v2,.v4}.md` therefore passes for a reason that generalises, and a self-test case pins it. A `.vN` on a *different* stem is still a collision — also pinned.

Deliberately **not** part of the rule: the records' `**Status**` lines. They are free prose (`Proposed`, `Draft (2026-05-24)`, `Accepted in part`, `Superseded by v4`) and a grep does not read status either — the navigation damage is the same whatever they say. Worth recording because the issue body describes all six records as "已接受": measured, only the `0057` pair is; `0019-app-as-consumer-unit` is Proposed and both `0010` records are Proposed/Draft. That changes nothing about the collision, which is what the ruling is about.

**2. The gate's own blind spot is closed.** The old inventory regex was `/^(\d{4})-/`, so a misnamed record (`0123_foo.md`) was silently invisible to it — and would be invisible to the number audit too. A `.md` file under `docs/adr/` must now parse as `NNNN-kebab-slug[.vN].md` or be declared a non-record in `NON_RECORD_FILES` (today: `PRIORITIZATION.md` only).

**3. A non-failing note.** On success the gate lists the anchor entries whose number is one of the ambiguous ones — 4 today, all `ADR-0057`. That is exactly the debt route B pays down; printing it keeps the size visible instead of leaving it to be rediscovered.

**4. The broken link is fixed — and it was not where the card said.**

The issue body and the triage comment both place it in `0057-system-data-lifecycle-and-retention.md`. Measured at `origin/main` `a36db28`, it is in the *other* `0057`:

- `docs/adr/0057-erp-authorization-core-business-units-and-scope-depth.md:5` held `[ADR-0010](./0010-metadata-protection.md)` — no such file; the record is `0010-metadata-protection-model.md`.
- `0057-system-data-lifecycle-and-retention.md` contains no `0010` reference at all.

The two sources agree only because the second inherited the first's reading. Fixed at the real location.

## Why the assertion lives in the script, not in `scripts/adr-anchors.json`

`adr-anchors.json` is a data map from *code files* to ADR ids, and its one `"//"` key says so. A directory-level exemption ledger is not an anchor: it would need a new top-level key, changing that file's contract, and JSON cannot carry the per-entry prose each grandfathered pair needs. There is also a governance reason — a PR that widens the allowlist has to edit **the gate**, which reads as a governance change in review; editing a data file reads as bookkeeping.

## Proof that the red path works

A gate whose red path was never exercised is not a gate, and this one's is rare by construction — someone has to introduce a fourth collision before anyone sees it fail. So it is provoked three ways.

**a. A real fourth collision in the working tree.** Added `docs/adr/0112-fourth-collision-probe.md` next to `0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md`, ran the gate, deleted it, re-ran:

```
check-adr-anchors: 1 problem(s)

  • docs/adr/: ADR number 0112 is claimed by 2 unrelated decisions —
        0112-error-code-vocabulary-and-ledger.md
        0112-fourth-collision-probe.md
      An ADR number must name exactly ONE decision. AGENTS.md Prime Directive #13 tells the next
      author to grep the ADRs for the id they found in the code; a shared number hands them two
      records and no way to choose, which is how an accepted decision gets reversed by someone who
      read the other one (#3723, the incident this whole file exists for).
      Fix: give the NEW record the next free number — 0123 — and update any reference you already
      wrote. Renumbering an ALREADY-ACCEPTED record was ruled out (#5992: 296+ bare references would
      migrate, and an accepted decision's number must not move), so before it is referenced is the
      only cheap moment.
      Successive versions of ONE decision are not a collision and do not belong here — they repeat
      the same stem and add `.vN` (see 0006-project-environment-split{,.v2,.v4}.md).
```

Exit 1. The message computes the next free number (`0123`) so the fix is mechanical, and a self-test assertion pins that the remedy offered is never "widen the allowlist". After deleting the probe: green again.

**b. Ablating the allowlist, against the live tree.** Ran the real script with only the `0057` entry removed (patched copy, same code path, repo root as cwd). **Predicted red, observed red** — one error naming both `0057` records. So the entries are load-bearing today rather than decorative.

**c. In-process and permanent.** `--self-test` runs the same `auditAdrDirectory()` over synthetic directories (clean / versions / new collision / allowlisted / third claimant / stale entry / unparseable filename / `.vN` on a different stem) **and** over the live `docs/adr/`, asserting it is green as shipped and that dropping the allowlist entirely yields exactly the three known collisions. If that ablation ever goes green, the allowlist has stopped being what keeps the build green and the entries are dead weight — which the assertion says by name.

Every assertion is named and the body is guarded, so an ablation reports which invariant broke rather than a stack trace. Under the probe in (a) the self-test failed with `live-tree-is-green-today` and `ablation-without-allowlist-is-red`, both named, exit 1.

The self-test is wired into the pnpm script (`--self-test && ` the real run), following `check:adr-0087-registration`, so CI runs it on every PR without a workflow change.

## CI wiring (verified, not assumed)

`check:adr-anchors` is `.github/workflows/lint.yml` line 186, inside the **ESLint** job — no paths filter, triggers on `pull_request`, `push: main` and `merge_group`, and ESLint is in the required set since #5617. A new collision therefore actually goes red on the PR and in the queue.

## Changeset

None — `skip-changeset`. This PR touches `scripts/check-adr-anchors.mjs`, the **private** root `package.json`'s script wiring, comments and a step name in `lint.yml`, and one link inside a `docs/adr/` record. No workspace package changes, nothing published, no runtime or authoring surface: it releases nothing, so a changeset would announce a release that does not exist.

## Gates run locally

`pnpm lint`, then every `check:*` step enumerated from `lint.yml` in order (30 of them, ESLint job) plus `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:driver-conformance`, `check:stall-guard` and the `check:generated --reconcile-only` meta-gate — all PASS. Run after `git commit`, since the ADR-family gates read the committed tree.

## Out of scope, reported not fixed

`docs/adr/` is **outside the `Check Links` gate's scan surface** — `check-links.yml` passes lychee `content/**/*.md`, `content/**/*.mdx` and `README.md` only. That is why the broken link above survived. Sweeping the directory for unresolved relative links found only that one genuine break; the two remaining hits are both `./crm_lead_guide.md` in `0046-package-docs-as-metadata.md`, which are *illustrative* — one inside a code span, one inside a fenced ` ```md ` block — demonstrating the package-docs link convention. So naively widening lychee's surface to `docs/adr/` would go red on documentation-of-a-convention. Filed as #6592 (`finding`, unassigned) rather than fixed here.
